description: Soy Dilan Yovani García, ingeniero de Morelos, México, y ando en muchas cosas a la vez. Estudio en el Tec de Zacatepec, donde con mi equipo de cinco preparo un protocolo de investigación sobre un sistema de monitoreo en tiempo real con GPS, ESP32 e IoT para las rutas de transporte público de la escuela. Al mismo tiempo trabajo y empleo en un rol de sistemas o devops. Ahí doy capacidades a clientes sobre su portal de servicios, lo puedo hasta encontrar errores y armo desde directores de contacto.
summary: Astronaut Health Monitor is an offline-first web tool that helps a crew member assess their own health during a mission and know what to do next, even when contact with Earth is delayed or unavailable. It runs on an on-board local server with no internet. The dashboard tracks 14 health indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, temperature, sleep, hydration, bone loss, muscle mass, radiation dose and more) against each person's baseline and shows every one as Normal, Caution or Critical. Each alert cites the NASA-STD-3001 or NASA HRP requirement behind it. A simulated "Flight Surgeon" assistant detects patterns such as possible hypoxia or fever, explains what to do, and can queue a message for the ground using the communication delay of the mission environment, from low Earth orbit to Mars. All data is simulated. The tool provides guidance only and does not diagnose.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

On long missions, communication with Earth can take up to 20 minutes each way, so crew members must be able to understand their own health status and act on it. Astronaut Health Monitor runs entirely on a local on-board server and gives each crew member a dashboard of 14 indicators compared with their personal baseline, a body figure, 7-day trends and a clear "What to do now" list. Every alert is traced to its source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 Rev. C requirements, NASA HRP observations, the project guide or a clinical reference, with revision and an "example value" label until reviewed by a medical professional. The 9 body-system sections of the reference document, plus metabolism and radiation, are shown as 11 systems; systems with no indicator yet are shown as "no coverage yet" instead of "normal".

A simulated Flight Surgeon assistant detects patterns (possible hypoxia, fever, dehydration, acute stress, irregular pulse, sleep loss, sensor failure), opens automatically, explains what to do using the guide and the crew member's 7-day history and record, and offers to alert the ground. It uses hypothesis language, never a diagnosis, and a deterministic safety filter blocks doses and definitive-diagnosis wording. Care levels 3 to 5 and the communication delay of each environment (space station, spacecraft, lunar base, Mars base) decide whether the ground is reached live or asynchronously through a ground queue.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

It supports crew autonomy where the ground cannot respond in time, keeps decisions traceable to public NASA standards, and works with no internet. The simulation engine produces labeled scenarios, so detection can be evaluated against known ground truth.

HOW IT WAS BUILT

Laravel 10, Livewire 3, MySQL, Laravel Reverb (live updates), Chart.js, Tailwind CSS and Vite, delivered as an installable offline-first web app. Security features include role-based access (crew member, Crew Medical Officer, Flight Surgeon), an access audit log without medical values, encrypted record fields, a token-authenticated and optionally signed wearable ingestion API, and a data-quality layer that flags suspect readings instead of rejecting them. More than 500 automated tests run against a separate test database.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It separates requirement layers (standard vs. HRP observation), is honest about uncovered systems, and combines live simulation, pattern detection and a conversational-style assistant that always escalates red-flag situations to the ground.

LIMITATIONS

All data is simulated and thresholds are unvalidated examples awaiting medical review. The interface is in English; some demo data may still appear in Spanish. A local AI model with n8n orchestration, more biomarkers and real wearable integration are on the roadmap. The tool provides guidance only and does not diagnose or prescribe. Not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
